record.summary: This record's geometry is the owner-identified footprint west of and adjacent to Third Street Garage on OCII plan Block 23A; that address and adjacency match the Joan and Sanford I. Weill Neurosciences Building at 1651 4th Street, a six-story, roughly 282,500-sq-ft neuroscience research and clinical building (design architect Mark Cavagnero Associates with SmithGroup as executive architect) that opened in October 2021. UCSF Health's own 'Neurosurgery Mission Bay - Fourth St.' clinic listing gives the same 1651 4th Street address.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- an idealized rectangle (owner-directed construction: real-gap-fragment shape cut and aligned to Third Street Garage's own real orientation), not a hand-traced or surveyed footprint. The building's identity (UCSF Neurosurgery at San Francisco Mission Bay) and adjacency to Third Street Garage are from the owner's direct knowledge; not independently corroborated by a primary source in this pass.

open_questions: This record's own geometry file notes the owner directly identified the building here as UCSF Neurosurgery at Mission Bay (correcting an earlier mis-resolution to Genentech Hall) but flags that identification as not independently corroborated by a primary source in that pass. This research pass found strong, independent corroboration: a contractor project page names this same OCII Block 23A as the site of the Joan and Sanford I. Weill Neurosciences Building, and UCSF Health's own clinic-location page places its 'Neurosurgery Mission Bay - Fourth St.' service at 1651 4th Street, the Weill building's address, directly adjacent to Third Street Garage as this record's geometry describes. Not treated as fully closed: no single source explicitly ties the parcel-level footprint to the 1651 4th Street address by lot number.

Exact opening day is not confirmed: this record uses October 2021 (from UCSF's own news article, dated by its URL and by architecture-press coverage of the same announcement); one secondary aggregation suggested October 28, 2021 specifically, but that day was not independently verified against a primary page in this pass.

Construction cost is reported elsewhere (via a $185 million naming gift from the Weill Family Foundation, and a total project value cited by some outlets around $535 million) but was not independently verified against a primary UCSF or Regents document in this pass, so left out of costs.
